tip.addBand: Add a flat band (up to {max}) · or double-click an empty spot on the graph
tip.addBand.full: This device supports up to {max} bands
tip.conn.missing: Device not found. Connect it, then choose “Read from device”
tip.sync: Compares the editor with the EQ last read from or applied to the device
tip.handle: {band} · Drag: frequency and gain · Wheel: Q · Double-click: 0 dB · Delete: remove
tip.type: Filter type (only the types this device supports are listed)
tip.field: Type a value or drag the label sideways · ↑↓ one step, Shift ×10
language.unsupported: System language ({locale}) is not supported; showing {lang}
app.title: Moondrop Control Panel
action.read.tip: Load the device's current EQ into the editor
action.apply.tip: Back up, then apply. Unplugging restores the last saved EQ
action.save.tip: Back up, apply, save to the device, and verify after reconnect
action.export: Export edited EQ as preset file…
status.read.missing: Device not found. Connect it and choose “Read from device”; for a model the app doesn't know yet, add a profile in Settings (⌘, / Ctrl+,)
status.apply.ok: Applied temporarily · unplugging restores the last saved EQ
status.apply.same: The device already has this EQ
status.save.busy: Applying and saving to the device… (the device restarts)
status.save.ok: Saved to the device and verified after reconnect
status.preset: Loaded preset “{title}”. Choose “Apply” or “Save to device” to send it
status.export.ok: Exported the edited EQ as a preset file
status.import.ok: Loaded the preset file into the editor. Apply it to send it to the device
status.tooManyBands: This device supports up to {max} bands. Remove {extra} and try again
band.name: Band {n}
band.empty: No bands. Choose “Add band” or double-click the graph
preset.chu2-quiet-18db.title: Quiet −18 dB
preset.chu2-quiet-18db.note: Lowers the overall level by about 18 dB while keeping the tonal balance close to stock. Listening-tested on a CHU II DSP; the curve comes from a software model, not a measurement.
tip.settings: Device, profiles, presets, AI assistant, and folders
status.read.snapshot: Read the EQ. First time with this model: its current EQ was saved as the “Original” preset
status.ai: Loaded the AI's EQ into the editor. Choose “Apply” to try it on the device
confirm.unverified.title: Unverified device profile
confirm.unverified: The profile for {device} has not been verified on real hardware. A backup is written first, and “Apply” is undone by unplugging, but a wrong register map can still misconfigure the device. Continue?
preset.flat.title: Flat (no bands)
preset.flat.note: Clears every band. The earphone plays its own tuning with no user EQ on top.
preset.original.title: Original · {device}
settings.title: Settings
dev.heading: Connected device
dev.none: No supported device found. Connect the earphone, or add a profile for your model below.
dev.profile.hint: A profile tells the app how to talk to one model. Automatic detection picks the profile whose USB vendor/product ID is connected. Choose one explicitly only if detection picks the wrong one.
hid.heading: USB devices on this computer
hid.hint: Your earphone shows up here as a HID device even when no profile knows it yet. The manufacturer name may be Moondrop or the DSP chip's vendor.
hid.empty: No candidate devices found. Connect the earphone directly (not through a charge-only cable or hub) and scan again.
hid.name: Device
hid.next: Next: “Create profile…” copies the template profile (chosen in Device profiles) with this device's IDs. Probe it read-only, then try a temporary Apply before saving.
pf.heading: Device profiles
pf.hint: Everything the app knows about a model: its USB IDs, register map, and value ranges. Built-in profiles can't be changed, but saving one creates a user copy that replaces it.
pf.pick: Pick a profile on the left, or create a new one.
pf.newHint: New profile from the template. Set the USB IDs (see the Device tab) and the register layout, then probe it.
pf.fromHid: Profile draft created from the USB device. Probe it read-only before saving.
pf.templateNote: Started from the {template} template; not verified on this model.
pf.imported: Imported. Review it, probe it, then save.
pf.duplicated: Copy created. Give it its own ID and save.
pf.probe.tip: Reads the registers this profile describes from the connected device and decodes them. Writes nothing.
pf.overwrite: A user profile with ID {id} exists. Replace it?
pf.using: This profile is now used instead of automatic detection
pf.builtinHint: Built-in profile. Saving creates a user copy with the same ID that replaces it; delete the copy to go back.
pf.title: Name
pf.verified: Verified on hardware (write, readback, and save all confirmed)
pf.s.usb.hint: From the Device tab. Set the usage page only if several HID interfaces share the vendor/product ID.
pf.s.protocol.hint: Command bytes and special registers. All byte values are hex.
pf.s.switch.hint: The register that turns the custom EQ on or off, and the value bytes a read of it needs.
pf.s.bands.hint: Band n uses the “registers per band” registers starting at first + n × stride. Their values, concatenated, are the band's bytes (see Band encoding).
pf.s.filters.hint: The byte the device uses for each filter type. Leave empty if the device lacks that type.
pf.s.unused.hint: Written to slots without a band. Must be 0 dB; slots holding exactly this read back as empty.
probe.ok: Probe: every register answered and decoded
probe.fail: Probe: some registers could not be read or decoded
issues.heading: Some files in the data folder could not be loaded:
preset.heading: Presets
preset.empty: No presets for this device yet.
preset.saveHeading: Save the edited EQ as a preset
preset.saveHint: Saves the EQ currently in the editor (including band colors) to the data folder. Nothing is sent to the device.
preset.title: Name
preset.overwrite: A preset with ID {id} exists. Replace it?
ai.heading: AI assistant
ai.hint: Works with any AI chat (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini…). The app writes a complete prompt with your device's limits; you paste the AI's answer back and the app checks it before using it.
ai.task.eq.hint: Describe the sound you want. The AI answers with a preset that fits this device; it is loaded into the editor, not sent to the device.
ai.task.profile.hint: The AI helps fill in a device profile for a Moondrop model the app doesn't know yet. Include the USB device list and a probe result.
ai.task.troubleshoot.hint: Describe what goes wrong. The prompt includes the connection state, the last message, and the profile.
ai.goal.eq: e.g. Slightly less bass, a bit more clarity in vocals, and 6 dB quieter overall
ai.goal.profile: e.g. My Moondrop model isn't detected; it appears in the USB list as VID:PID …
ai.goal.troubleshoot: e.g. Apply works, but Save to device fails after the earphone restarts
ai.copied: Prompt copied. Paste it into your AI chat.
ai.reply.placeholder: Paste the whole answer; the app finds the JSON block
ai.loaded.eq: Loaded into the editor. Choose “Apply” to try it; unplugging restores the saved EQ.
ai.loaded.preset: Loaded into the editor. Choose “Apply” to try it, and save it as a preset in the Presets tab (name and note are filled in).
ai.loaded.profile: The AI's profile is open in the editor. Probe it (read-only) before saving.
ai.invalid: The AI's EQ does not fit this device: {problems}. Ask the AI to fix it.
ai.docs: The prompt templates are in docs/ai/ in the project, for use without the app as well.
check.gain: band {n}: gain {value} dB is outside {min} to {max}
check.freq: band {n}: frequency {value} Hz is outside {min} to {max}
check.type: band {n}: this device has no {type} filter
adv.heading: Advanced
adv.warning: Expert tools. These write straight to the device without a backup; export the EQ first. Wrong values can misconfigure the device until it is reset.
adv.noDevice: Connect a device to use these tools.
adv.pregain.hint: The register reads and writes, but whether it changes the sound is unverified.
adv.pregain.written: Pregain register set to {db} dB (not saved to the device)
adv.badPregain: Enter a whole number from -128 to 127
adv.raw.hint: A whole report in hex (the profile's report length, report ID first). Shows the device's response.
adv.commit: Save current settings to the device
adv.commit.hint: Sends the profile's save command. The device restarts; read it again afterwards to check.
adv.commit.confirm: Save the device's current settings permanently? The device will restart.
adv.committed: Save command sent. Read from the device after it reconnects to check.
adv.confirm: Write directly to the device without a backup?
gen.heading: General
gen.data.hint: User profiles, presets, snapshots, and settings. Shared with the command line tool. Share a profile by exporting it, or send the JSON file from here.
gen.backup.hint: Before every change, the device's EQ is saved here as a JSON file you can import again.
gen.capture: Save a model's EQ the first time it is connected
gen.snapshot.hint: Kept as the “Original” preset so you can always go back to how the device came. Delete it in Presets to capture it again.
tip.eq.always: This device has no EQ on/off switch; its EQ is always on
pf.s.frame.hint: Byte positions in each report (byte 0 is the report ID; the rest are zero unless set). A response repeats the first “echo length” bytes and carries the 4-byte value at the value offset.
pf.hasSwitch: The device has an EQ on/off register
pf.s.timing.hint: How long to wait for answers and for the device to come back after saving; the sample rate only affects the response graph.
probe.noSwitch: No EQ switch in this profile (always on)
gen.udev.hint: On Linux, a udev rule lets you open the earphone without root. These rules cover the USB vendor of every known profile, including your own.
pf.s.encoding.hint: Where gain, frequency, Q and the filter code sit in the band's bytes, and their units (wire value = value ÷ step). Bytes no field covers are written as 0 and must read back as 0.
